notApplicable.hdt045: HDT is a rigid-bar test. ISO 75 ends at 0.2 % outer-fibre strain, which a bar reaches once its modulus falls to about 225 MPa, so an elastomer has no meaningful HDT and makers list it as N/A. A value an elastomer's sheet publishes is shown and never decides. Sintering filaments are left out too: the finished part is the sintered metal or ceramic.

items.text: Conductive Filaflex TPU is a flexible, electrically conductive filament developed for the production of conductive components and wearable electronic devices.
Its unique material formulation makes it suitable for both prototyping and end-use parts in low-current applications where flexibility and conductivity are required.
Flexible Electronics: Conductive tracks, contacts, and pressure-sensitive buttons
Wearable Technology: Direct printing on textiles and flexible wearable components
Medical Applications: ECG patches and flexible monitoring devices
Functional Prototyping: Low-current conductive components
This innovative filament opens new possibilities in the creation of functional electronic components and wearable devices, making it a game-changer for both prototyping and end-use applications.
The filament's electrical resistance can be fine-tuned through printing parameters, making it ideal for low-current applications where precision and reliability are crucial.
Flexible Electronics: Conductive circuits and pressure-sensitive buttons
Wearable Tech: Direct printing on textiles
Interactive Devices: Arduino keyboards, trackpads, joysticks
Medical Applications: ECG patches and monitoring devices
Conductive Filaflex TPU filament is an electrically conductive flexible filament, ideal for manufacturing electrically conductive parts or components and for creating wearable devices.
Dual Properties: Electrical conductivity combined with flexible TPU behavior
Conductive Filaflex TPU is a groundbreaking material in the world of flexible 3D printing, featuring a unique combination of electrical conductivity and flexibility with a precise 92A Shore hardness.
With its optimal hardness level, Conductive Filaflex ensures exceptional compatibility with 90% of market-available 3D printers, eliminating the need for specialized hardware.
Dual Properties: Electrical conductivity with flexibility
Wide Compatibility: Works with 90% of 3D printers
Please note that this filament is engineered specifically for low-current applications; exceeding these limits may affect performance or part integrity.
Poor adhesion 1. Dry the filament 2. Use adhesive 3. Adjust first layer
Drying is crucial for optimal results
Filament Drying (CRUCIAL): 📏 Temperature: 55°C ⏱️ Minimum time: 1 hour
Proper drying is essential for optimal printing results
Keep filament dry - store properly and dry before use
Easy Printing: No hardened nozzle required
Designed with user-friendliness in mind, this filament prints seamlessly without requiring a hardened nozzle and is safe for most printers.
Easy Printing: No hardened nozzle needed, safe for most printers
Print multiple small parts simultaneously for better results.
Use maximum travel speed to minimize stringing.
To ensure superior surface finish and optimal layer adhesion, it is recommended to utilize reduced printing speeds in accordance with the specified parameters.
A thorough extruder purge is mandatory after each material change to prevent cross-contamination and ensure the consistency of the filament’s mechanical and conductive properties.
When integrating Conductive Filaflex into electronic applications, the electrical resistance of the circuit must be calculated and verified.
We recommend a simple maintenance routine of cleaning with PET-G after use to ensure consistent, high-quality prints and prolonged printer life.
Simple Maintenance: Basic cleaning with PET-G after use
Unlike rigid filaments, this conductive TPU stretches when extruded, producing thinner lines.
The line width will be smaller than the nozzle diameter.
To ensure proper conductivity and bonding between vertical walls and perimeters, adjust flow and temperature accordingly.
Set travel speed to the maximum your machine allows (200-500mm/s).
Faster movements reduce filament oozing time, minimizing stringing.
Cooling Configuration: General: 0% (fan off) KEEP FAN ALWAYS: OFF Force fan speed for overhangs and bridges: OFF Layers < 10 seconds: 40% fan First layer: Always 0%
Irregular extrusion 1. Dry the filament 2. Check extruder 3. Reduce speed
Stringing 1. Dry the filament 2. Adjust retraction 3. Increase travel speed 4. Check temperature
Preferably use direct drive extruder

items.text: Eel is a low-conductivity material perfect for robotic manufacturing or small LEDs.

From cosplay LED gloves to wearable devices, there’s a lot you can create with Eel’s conductivity.
Truly flexible conductive material
355% elongation allows for repeated movement without wear or cracking

Eel's 355% elongation allows for repeated movement without wear or cracking.
NinjaTek's Eel filament is chemical resistant to a variety of materials.
The consistent diameter yields high-quality prints, and it’s chemically resistant to a variety of materials.
You'll produce reliable, high-quality prints due to the consistent diameter.
Glue is suggested on bed.

items.text: Ketones such as acetone, methylethylketone (MEK) and cyclohexanone are partial solvents for thermoplastic polyurethane elastomers. Elastollan products are unsuitable for long-term use in these solvents. Methyl ethyl ketone: volume swelling 105 % / 110 % / 130 %, reduction of tensile strength 80 % / 80 % / 90 % (ester / C 85 A / ether); other short-chained aliphatic ketones such as acetone have a similar effect.

items.text: Aliphatic alcohols, such as ethanol and isopropanol, cause swelling of Elastollan products. This is combined with a loss of tensile strength. items.text: No reduction in strength occurs after immersion in test oils IRM 901, IRM 902, and IRM 903 at room temperature. There is also no reduction in tensile strength after 3 weeks immersion at 100 °C. Elastollan is in principal resistant to lubricating oils and greases, however irreversible damage can be caused by included additives. Compatibility testing in each individual lubricant is to be recommended.

items.agent: Saturated hydrocarbons (diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether, kerosene)
items.text: Contact of Elastollan with saturated hydrocarbons such as diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether and kerosene results in a limited swelling. At room temperature, this swelling amounts to approx. 1-3 % and the resultant reduction in tensile strength is no more than 20 %. After evaporation and reversal of the swelling, the original mechanical properties are almost completely restored.

items.agent: Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU)
items.text: If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. This results in a reduction in mechanical properties. This effect is more marked in flexible grades. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.

items.text: Plastics are chemically degraded by the effect of UV radiation. The degree of ageing depends on duration and intensity. In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.
